state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The negative-sloping section on the distance-time graph represents Fido moving away from his home. Remember, on a distance-time graph, a negative slope indicates movement in the opposite direction. Make sure to correctly interpret the direction of movement when analyzing graphs.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, I see! So the negative slope means Fido is actually moving back towards home instead of falling asleep. But what does it mean when the graph is flat? Does that mean he's just standing still or resting?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: When the graph is flat on a distance-time graph, it means that Fido is at a constant distance from his home. It does not necessarily mean he is standing still or resting. Remember to consider the context of the situation when interpreting the graph.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher provides mathematically incorrect information (claiming negative slope means moving away when it actually means returning home, and incorrectly stating flat means constant distance rather than rest), fails to engage the student's specific misconception about confusing rest with movement, simply tells answers rather than prompting reasoning, and while the student shows some progress in Turn 2 by correctly interpreting the negative slope, this appears to be despite rather than because of the teacher's incorrect guidance.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently provides direct corrective feedback on the student's misconceptions and states explicit rules for interpreting distance-time graphs, though they could have been slightly more procedural by breaking down the interpretation steps more systematically.
